text: If you want to lower high cholesterol.
Simple changes to your diet can help.
Eating too many foods that are high in saturated fat
can raise your cholesterol.
These foods are high in saturated fat
so it's best to eat less of them.

Fatty and processed meats
such as beef, lamb, sausages and bacon.
Butter, lard and ghee
plus full fat milk, cheese and cream.
Tropical oils such as palm and coconut.

Baked goods like pastries,
pies, biscuits and cakes.

You can also check traffic light
labeling on food packs for saturates.
Red means high in saturated fat,
so try to cut back on these foods.

Eggs, shellfish, and organ meat
such as liver and kidney

contain a type of cholesterol
known as dietary cholesterol.

But this is different from
the cholesterol in your blood.

Research shows that dietary cholesterol
has only a small effect on blood cholesterol
so most people can enjoy eggs, shellfish, and organ meats
as part of a healthy diet.

What matters more is
cutting back on saturated fats.

If you have a genetic condition
called familial hypercholesterolemia,

you may still need to be careful about
dietary cholesterol in foods like eggs.

Some foods can help to bring
your cholesterol down.

Unsaturated fats such as
olive or vegetable oils,
an foods high in fibre like oats and barley
beans and lentils
nuts and seeds
fruit and vegetables.
